candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — carbamazepine pregnancy risk
candidate.educational_objective: Counsel clients that carbamazepine use during pregnancy is associated with increased risk of major congenital malformations, including neural tube defects, without presenting the outcome as inevitable.

options.A: Carbamazepine exposure is associated with an increased risk of major congenital malformations, including neural tube defects
options.B: Carbamazepine has no known fetal risk when used during pregnancy
options.C: The medication causes only maternal adverse effects and does not cross the placenta
options.D: Every exposed fetus will develop a neural tube defect

candidate.rationale: Current DailyMed labeling states that carbamazepine can cause fetal harm and that pregnancy-registry and epidemiologic data suggest an association with major congenital malformations, including neural tube defects. Therefore A is correct. The risk is increased but not inevitable. The label also recommends dietary folic acid supplementation before conception and during pregnancy, while noting that it is not known whether supplementation specifically reduces carbamazepine-associated neural tube defects.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Carbamazepine can cause fetal harm and is associated with an increased risk of major congenital malformations, including neural tube defects.
